concept.name: Tenkan-sen
concept.definition: The fastest Ichimoku line: the midpoint of the 9-period high-low range, (9-period high + 9-period low)/2, used as the short-term equilibrium level and the faster line in Ichimoku crossover signals.
concept.intuition: Rather than averaging closes, it averages the range extremes, so it sits at the center of recent price action and flattens immediately when the market goes quiet.
concept.mechanics: Compute (max(High,9) + min(Low,9))/2 each bar. A Tenkan cross above Kijun-sen is the classic bullish momentum signal (and below, bearish), conventionally filtered by price position relative to the cloud.
concept.failure_modes: As a 9-period range midpoint it moves in steps whenever the extreme bar rolls out of the window, and it whipsaws around Kijun-sen in flat markets.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a 9-period moving average of closes - it tracks the range midpoint, so it behaves differently (steppy, bounded by extremes) from an SMA or EMA.
concept.example: If the last 9 bars posted a highest high of 108 and a lowest low of 100, Tenkan-sen = 104.
